review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its one @[simp] lemma (chartRiemannianVolume_restrict_source) and the overlap theorem are used downstream in Volume.lean. I also checked that Mathlib's extChartAt_source exists. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The simp lemma is oriented correctly, since the RHS is strictly simpler. I did not flag the absence of a simp attribute on chartRiemannianVolume_apply, because it has a measurability hypothesis. The finding below is a normal-form mismatch. I did not run Lean and did not check whether extChartAt_source carries @[simp] (my grep output did not show attributes). The Volume.lean proof applies it explicitly, so the mismatch is real either way, but the 'simp-normal' claim depends on that attribute. Isometry.lean was only grepped for uses, not read in full.

findings.problem: The sibling simp lemma chartRiemannianVolume_restrict_source (line 235) states its restriction set as `(chartAt H α).source`. This overlap theorem states the set with `(extChartAt I α).source`, and `extChartAt_source` rewrites that to `(chartAt H α).source`. The two interface lemmas therefore use different forms of the same set, so they cannot be combined without first rewriting by `extChartAt_source`. The only downstream use of the overlap theorem, in Volume.lean, needs `simpa only [extChartAt_source] using chartRiemannianVolume_restrict_overlap (I := I) α β` to convert it to the chartAt form. The same file also converts back and forth with `simp only [extChartAt_source, ...]` (in restrict_source) and `simpa only [e, extChartAt_source]` (in the positivity lemma).
findings.proposed_change: State the theorem with chartAt sources, `(chartRiemannianVolume (I := I) α).restrict ((chartAt H α).source ∩ (chartAt H β).source) = (chartRiemannianVolume (I := I) β).restrict (...)`. Do the one conversion with `extChartAt_source` inside the proof, for example `simp only [← extChartAt_source I α, ← extChartAt_source I β]` at the start, or `rw` it into the existing body. Then drop the `simpa only [extChartAt_source]` wrapper in Volume.lean. Consider the same change for the `(extChartAt I α).source` occurrences in the statement of chartRiemannianVolume_apply, if the downstream uses allow it.
findings.benefit: The public lemmas then share one set-expression form, matching the simp-normal form that the @[simp] lemma chartRiemannianVolume_restrict_source already uses. Clients such as Volume.lean no longer need a manual `extChartAt_source` rewrite, and the overlap theorem stays stable under `simp`.
